title: Classification / Odd One Out — In-Depth Guide — Part 5 of 16

questions.question: What does 'Reverse Alphabet Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of letters or letter pairs share a reverse-alphabet (mirror) relationship, with one breaking it
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group shares a reverse-alphabet (mirror) relationship, identifying the letter or pair that doesn't follow that same mirrored pattern.

questions.question: What does 'Word-Length Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of words share a common letter count, with one word having a different length
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of words all share the same total letter count, identifying the one word with a different length.

questions.question: How does 'Letter Count Classification' relate to Word-Length Classification?
options: They test the same underlying property — the number of letters in each word
Letter count only applies to numbers
Word length ignores letter count entirely
questions.rationale: Both terms describe the same underlying idea: classifying based on how many letters each word contains.

questions.question: What does 'Repeated-Letter Classification' test?
options: Whether words are all the same length
Whether a group of words all contain a repeated letter, with one word having no repeated letters (or vice versa)
Whether words share the same first letter
questions.rationale: This tests whether words share the property of containing a repeated letter, identifying the one word that breaks that shared pattern.

questions.question: What does 'Unique-Letter Classification' test, in contrast?
options: The same property as repeated-letter classification
Whether a group of words all have entirely unique (non-repeating) letters, with one word breaking that pattern
Whether words share the same length
questions.rationale: This tests the opposite property from repeated-letter classification — whether every letter in each word is unique, with no repeats — identifying the exception.

questions.question: What does 'Alphabetical Order Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of words' letters are arranged in alphabetical order internally, with one word breaking that pattern
questions.rationale: This tests whether each word's own letters appear in alphabetical order (like 'aim'), identifying the one word that doesn't follow this internal ordering.

questions.question: What does 'Reverse Alphabetical Order' classification test, similarly?
options: The same property as alphabetical order
Whether each word's letters appear in REVERSE alphabetical order internally, with one word breaking that pattern
questions.rationale: This tests whether each word's own letters appear in reverse alphabetical order, identifying the exception that doesn't follow this pattern.

questions.question: What does 'Word Semantic Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of words share a common meaning-based category, with one word belonging to a different meaning category
questions.rationale: This tests whether words share a common meaning-based (semantic) category, identifying the one word whose meaning doesn't fit that shared category.

questions.question: What does 'Synonym Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of words are all synonyms (similar meaning) of each other, with one word not sharing that meaning
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of words are all synonyms of each other, identifying the one word whose meaning doesn't match the shared synonym group.

questions.question: What does 'Antonym Classification' test, in contrast?
options: A group where most items form opposite-meaning pairs, with one item breaking that antonym pattern
questions.rationale: This tests a pattern based on opposite (antonym) meanings among the group, identifying the item that breaks the expected antonym relationship.
